items.title: Legal encounters may offer overlooked opportunities for suicide prevention, analysis suggests
items.summary: Picture a forlorn man walking into a lawyer's office after his marriage has collapsed. The bank is threatening foreclosure, and his finances are in tatters. His problems may be legal on paper, but in person they can look far more complicated: panic, shame or the numb resignation of someone who can no longer imagine a way out. He did not come for counseling, and his lawyer is not a therapist. Still, the attorney may be sitting beside him at the worst moment of his life—with a chance to help before despair slides into tragedy.

items.title: Sapphire-grown semiconductor film sets bandgap record
items.summary: Semiconductors with wider bandgaps could pave the way for smaller, more efficient electronics that can handle far higher voltages, but the wider this gap becomes, the harder it is to control how well a material conducts electricity. Now, a team led by Darrell Schlom at Cornell University has shown that adding silicon to thin films of aluminum gallium oxide can keep this control intact at bandgaps wider than any semiconductor before it. Their research has been published in Nature.

items.title: Grèce: «Comme en France», étudiants, professeurs et fonctionnaires manifestent contre les conditions d'enseignement
items.summary: Outre la France, la révolte des étudiants gagne aussi la Grèce. Mercredi 21 octobre, des manifestations ont eu lieu dans plusieurs villes du pays pour réclamer davantage de moyens pour l’éducation, mais aussi pour protester contre le coût de la vie et les difficultés d’accès au logement. Plus de 10 000 étudiants, lycéens et enseignants se sont rassemblés dans le centre d’Athènes. Signe d’une grogne sociale qui gagne du terrain, alors que le gouvernement grec vante ses résultats économiques.

Deux ex-otages européennes enlevées au Niger en 2025 ont été libérées et se trouvent en Libye
items.summary: Eva Gretzmacher et Claudia Abbt, deux Européennes enlevées au Sahel en 2025, sont libres, a annoncé une chaîne de télévision libyenne. L'annonce a été confirmée jeudi 22 octobre grâce à des images des deux ex-otages arrivées à Benghazi. Car c'est par l'entremise de l’homme fort de l'est libyen, le maréchal Khalifa Haftar, qu'elles ont recouvré la liberté. L'Autrichienne Eva Gretzmacher avait été enlevée le 12 janvier 2025 à Agadez, dans le nord du Niger, où trois mois plus tard la Suisso-Nigérienne Claudia Abbt subissait le même sort. Elles étaient probablement aux mains des jihadistes du grou

items.title: Baby manta rays hunker down close to coasts before facing the open ocean's dangers
items.summary: Giant manta rays can grow up to nine meters (30 feet) long with a disk size of seven meters (23 feet) across and weigh up to 2,000 kg (4,400 pounds). This size leaves them with very few natural enemies once they reach adulthood at around eight to 10 years old. But giant manta ray babies, called pups, cannot rely on their size to protect them from predators that live in the open ocean, including several species of shark and orcas.

Massive boulders form the tomb, including the heaviest capstone ever used in a Dutch dolmen, estimated to weigh around 20 tons. The monument has fascinated visitors for centuries. items.title: [Perspectives] Beyond the battlefield: war and global health security
items.summary: During the Syrian war (2011–24), the Assad Government forces and their Russian allies conducted hundreds of strikes on medical facilities in opposition-held areas. Monitoring groups documented over 600 attacks on health care, resulting in the deaths of hundreds of health-care workers throughout the conflict. Hospitals in eastern Aleppo and other contested regions were reduced to rubble. Surgeons operated in underground rooms illuminated by generators, and ambulances were targeted while transporting patients between sites.

items.title: [Perspectives] Temporal rationing: a man with gastric cancer in Colombia
items.summary: Pepe, a 45-year-old man living in the city of Cali, Colombia, worked as a self-employed hauler of goods with a wheelbarrow. In 2010, he presented to a general practitioner with several months of abdominal heaviness and non-exertional substernal burning. The physician provisionally diagnosed gastro-oesophageal reflux disease and prescribed omeprazole. items.title: Milton College in Milton, Wisconsin
items.summary: When Milton College finally closed its doors in 1982, it was the oldest institution of higher education in Wisconsin, beating the University of Wisconsin by four years. The college was originally called Du Lac Academy when it was founded in 1844. Main Hall and Goodrich Hall (the original dorm) – built in 1855 and 1857, respectively – are still standing. Milton College was ahead of its time in admitting women. It was a coeducational institution from the start. items.title: [Editorial] Rethinking threats to human survival
items.summary: Much health advocacy is driven by single-issue activism. Communities with a common interest—from AIDS to child health, climate to tobacco control—focus intensely on their own domain. And understandably so. Important progress has been made through often courageous direct action. But this sharply competitive approach is, according to a new Lancet Commission on 21st Century Global Threats to Health, dangerously flawed. Indeed, perhaps the most important contribution of this Commission is to move global health beyond the consideration of individual harms.

items.title: [Editorial] Rethinking lived experience
items.summary: The theme of this year's World Mental Health Day, held on Oct 10, is Lived experiences heard: real voices, real change. On its website, WHO states that the voices of people with lived experience should “shape the policies, services and decisions that affect their lives”. While these are laudable aims, they also serve to highlight the complex challenges involved in lived experience engagement and co-production, both within the field of mental health and beyond.

items.title: [Comment] Retatrutide in adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes: what have we learned from TRIUMPH-2?
items.summary: It is a general observation that the degree of weight loss obtained with GLP-1 receptor agonists is less in individuals with type 2 diabetes than in people without diabetes and similar BMI. Could this difference be overcome with the new triple agonists with superior weight-lowering effects?
